/cli: Forge in the terminal, by category

A settings row in the menu that lists every flag and subcommand, one tab per category. The window is 80 × 24, dark first, drawn from the app’s own art. The box, its bar and its keys are the menu popup’s, as /about’s are.

Decided

  • It is a settings row, and it opens inside the menu’s box like /about.
  • Grouped by category, one tab each. The README stays the full reference; this lists names and one line each, not every behaviour.
  • The rows are generated from the same table --help reads, so a new flag cannot be forgotten (a build detail, not on screen).

Open questions

  1. How does a row read? A, B or C below, pick one. I recommend C.
  2. Does ↵ copy the example? In C it does. It would use the clipboard code the shell already has. Say if you would rather it only be read.
  3. The name and its menu line. I used /cli, and “run Forge from the terminal” on its row (the word “commands” is kept for the menu’s own entries). Both strings are mine.
  4. The six tab names. Convert, Edit, PDF, Media, Tools, Setup. “Tools” holds probe, palette, scale, clip, watch and transcribe; “Setup” holds config, extensions, update, uninstall and mcp. Every tab name and row string on this page is mine, to be approved before it is built.
  5. /right-click and /theme. Neither has a command of its own (the theme is forge config set theme), so they have no row. Leave them out, or add a line for each in Setup?

SCREEN: the menu with the new row

The row sits after /right-click. Only the chosen row says what it does, as every row does.
